questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as used in genetics:

(i) Allele

(ii) Phenotype

(iii)Heterozygous. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **allele** is **one of the alternative forms of a gene**, occupying the same position (locus) on homologous chromosomes. *Example:* the alleles for tall (T) and short (t) in pea plants.

(ii) The **phenotype** is the **observable (physical or physiological) characteristic of an organism**, resulting from its genotype and the effect of the environment. *Example:* tall plant, blood group A.

(iii) **Heterozygous** describes an organism (or genotype) that has **two different alleles of a gene** for a given characteristic. *Example:* Tt (also called a hybrid).

questions.enonce_markdown: Sickle-cell anaemia is an inherited disease caused by a gene mutation on the haemoglobin molecule. Using suitable symbols and genetic diagrams, determine the genotypes, phenotypes and probability of the offspring of a man who is a carrier of sickle -cell trait and who marries a normal non - carrier woman. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Symbols:** $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ = allele for normal haemoglobin; $\mathrm{Hb^S}$ = allele for sickle-cell haemoglobin.

* Carrier man (sickle-cell trait): $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}$ (heterozygous)
* Normal non-carrier woman: $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}$ (homozygous normal)

**Genetic diagram**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parental phenotypes** | Carrier man $\times$ normal woman |
| **Parental genotypes** | $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}$ $\times$ $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}$ |
| **Gametes** | $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ or $\mathrm{Hb^S}$ (man); $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ (all, woman) |

**Punnett square**

| | $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ (woman) | $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ (woman) |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathrm{Hb^A}$ (man) | $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}$ | $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}$ |
| $\mathrm{Hb^S}$ (man) | $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}$ | $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}$ |

**Offspring**

| Genotype | Phenotype | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}$ | Normal (not a carrier) | 50 % ($\tfrac{1}{2}$) |
| $\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}$ | Normal but a carrier (sickle-cell trait) | 50 % ($\tfrac{1}{2}$) |
| $\mathrm{Hb^S Hb^S}$ | Sickle-cell anaemia | 0 % |

Ratio 1 normal : 1 carrier. **None of the children will suffer from sickle-cell anaemia**, but half of them will be carriers.
